title: 1 Kings Chapter 15 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 1 Kings chapter 15 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 1 Kings Chapter 15 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 1 Kings Chapter 15.

questions.question: In which year of King Jeroboam's reign did Abijam begin to reign over Judah?
questions.correctAnswer: Eighteenth year
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 15:1 states that Abijam began to reign over Judah in the eighteenth year of King Jeroboam.

questions.question: How many years did Abijam reign in Jerusalem?
questions.correctAnswer: Three years
questions.explanation: According to 1 Kings 15:2, Abijam reigned three years in Jerusalem.

questions.question: What was the name of Abijam's mother?
questions.correctAnswer: Maachah
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 15:2 tells us Abijam's mother was Maachah, the daughter of Abishalom.

questions.question: True or False: Abijam's heart was perfect with the LORD like David's.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 15:3 states that Abijam's heart was not perfect with the LORD his God as David's heart was.

questions.question: Why did the LORD give Abijam a lamp in Jerusalem?
options: For David's sake to set up his son after him and establish Jerusalem
Because Abijam was a righteous king
questions.correctAnswer: For David's sake to set up his son after him and establish Jerusalem
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 15:4 explains the LORD gave Abijam a lamp in Jerusalem for David's sake to set up his son after him and to establish Jerusalem.

questions.question: True or False: David turned aside from the LORD's commandments many times during his life.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 15:5 says David did that which was right and turned not aside from any thing that the LORD commanded all his life, except in the matter of Uriah the Hittite.

questions.question: Who was at war all their days according to 1 Kings 15:6?
questions.correctAnswer: Rehoboam and Jeroboam
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 15:6 states that there was war between Rehoboam and Jeroboam all their days.

questions.question: What was written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah besides what is mentioned in the chapter?
options: The rest of the acts of Abijam and all that he did
questions.correctAnswer: The rest of the acts of Abijam and all that he did
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 15:7 refers to the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah containing the rest of the acts of Abijam and all that he did.

questions.question: Who reigned after Abijam's death?
questions.correctAnswer: Asa
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 15:8 explains that after Abijam died, Asa his son reigned in his stead.

questions.question: True or False: Asa reigned over Judah starting in the twentieth year of Jeroboam's reign.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 15:9 states Asa began to reign in the twentieth year of Jeroboam king of Israel.

questions.question: How long did Asa reign in Jerusalem?
questions.correctAnswer: Forty-one years
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 15:10 says Asa reigned forty-one years in Jerusalem.

questions.question: What did Asa do that was right in the eyes of the LORD?
options: He removed sodomites and idols his fathers made
questions.correctAnswer: He removed sodomites and idols his fathers made
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 15:12 records Asa took away the sodomites and removed all idols made by his fathers.

questions.question: Who was taken away from being queen because she made an idol in a grove?
questions.correctAnswer: Maachah
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 15:13 states Asa removed his mother Maachah from being queen because she made an idol in a grove.

questions.question: True or False: Asa's heart was perfect with the LORD all his days despite not removing the high places.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 15:14 says Asa's heart was perfect with the LORD all his days even though the high places were not removed.

questions.question: In 1 Kings 15, which event happened first?
questions.correctAnswer: Abijam began to reign
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 15:1 introduces Abijam's reign first before later events such as Asa's reign and removal of idols.

medium.title: 1 Kings Chapter 15 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 1 Kings Chapter 15 to real-life situations.

questions.question: Why did King Asa remove his mother Maachah from being queen?
options: Because she made an idol in a grove
Because she was unfaithful to the LORD
Because she supported Baasha king of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: Because she made an idol in a grove
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 15:13 states Asa removed Maachah from being queen because she had made an idol in a grove. This shows Asa's commitment to removing idolatry from Judah, as also seen in his actions in verses 12 and 13.

questions.question: What was the condition of Asa's heart despite not removing the high places?
options: His heart was perfect with the LORD all his days
His heart was divided between God and idols
His heart was hardened against God
His heart was full of doubt
questions.correctAnswer: His heart was perfect with the LORD all his days
questions.explanation: According to 1 Kings 15:14, although Asa did not remove the high places, his heart was perfect with the LORD all his days. This indicates his sincere devotion despite incomplete reforms.

questions.question: What did Asa bring into the house of the LORD?
options: Silver, gold, and vessels dedicated by himself and his father
Only silver dedicated by the people
questions.correctAnswer: Silver, gold, and vessels dedicated by himself and his father
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 15:15 describes that Asa brought into the house of the LORD the silver, gold, and vessels dedicated by himself and his father, showing his dedication to honoring God.

questions.question: What was the nature of the relationship between Asa king of Judah and Baasha king of Israel during their reigns?
options: There was war between them all their days
questions.correctAnswer: There was war between them all their days
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 15:16 states explicitly there was war between Asa and Baasha king of Israel all their days, indicating ongoing conflict.

questions.question: What strategic action did Baasha king of Israel take against Judah?
options: He built Ramah to block entry and exit to Asa
He formed an alliance with Judah
He built a fortress at Geba
questions.correctAnswer: He built Ramah to block entry and exit to Asa
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 15:17 reveals Baasha built Ramah to prevent any from going out or coming in to Asa king of Judah, a defensive and offensive tactic.

questions.question: How did Asa respond to Baasha's construction of Ramah?
options: He sent silver and gold to Benhadad king of Syria to form an alliance
He built a wall around Jerusalem
questions.correctAnswer: He sent silver and gold to Benhadad king of Syria to form an alliance
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 15:18-19 shows Asa took treasures from the house of the LORD and the king's house and sent them to Benhadad, king of Syria, asking him to break his league with Baasha, thus responding diplomatically.

questions.question: What was the result of Asa's alliance with Benhadad against Baasha?
options: Benhadad attacked cities of Israel, forcing Baasha to stop building Ramah
The alliance led to peace between Israel and Judah
questions.correctAnswer: Benhadad attacked cities of Israel, forcing Baasha to stop building Ramah
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 15:20-21 narrates that Benhadad hearkened to Asa, attacked Israelite cities, and Baasha stopped building Ramah and dwelt in Tirzah.

questions.question: What action did King Asa take after Baasha stopped building Ramah?
options: He made a proclamation and used the stones and timber from Ramah to build Geba and Mizpah
questions.correctAnswer: He made a proclamation and used the stones and timber from Ramah to build Geba and Mizpah
questions.explanation: According to 1 Kings 15:22, Asa proclaimed throughout Judah to remove the stones and timber from Ramah and used them to build Geba and Mizpah, repurposing enemy fortifications.

questions.question: What does 1 Kings 15:23 teach us about Asa's later life despite his earlier faithfulness?
options: He was diseased in his feet in old age
He became king of Israel as well
questions.correctAnswer: He was diseased in his feet in old age
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 15:23 records that in Asa's old age he was diseased in his feet, showing that even faithful leaders experience physical struggles, a reminder of human frailty.

questions.question: Who succeeded Asa as king of Judah?
questions.correctAnswer: Jehoshaphat his son
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 15:24 clearly states that after Asa died, Jehoshaphat his son reigned in his stead, continuing the Davidic line.

questions.question: Based on 1 Kings 15:13-14, how does this passage teach us about the importance of wholehearted devotion to God despite incomplete reforms?
options: Asa's heart was perfect with the LORD all his days even though he did not remove all high places
Asa was punished for not removing the high places
Only complete removal of idols pleases God
Partial obedience is equal to disobedience
questions.correctAnswer: Asa's heart was perfect with the LORD all his days even though he did not remove all high places
questions.explanation: Verses 13-14 show Asa removed his mother's idol but did not remove the high places, yet his heart remained perfect with the LORD, teaching that sincere devotion matters greatly even if reforms are incomplete.

questions.question: A fellow believer struggles with trusting God during conflict. Based on Asa's response to Baasha's aggression (1 Kings 15:17-22), what biblical truth can encourage them?
options: Trusting God can include wise alliances and proactive steps to overcome opposition
Ignoring enemies is the best course of action
One should never seek help from others
questions.correctAnswer: Trusting God can include wise alliances and proactive steps to overcome opposition
questions.explanation: Asa trusted God but also sent treasures to Benhadad to break Baasha's alliance (verses 18-19) and then took practical steps to rebuild Judah's defenses (verse 22), showing faith involves wise action.

questions.question: True or False: Asa destroyed the idol made by his mother Maachah and burned it by the brook Kidron.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 15:13 explicitly states Asa destroyed the idol made by Maachah and burnt it by the brook Kidron, demonstrating his commitment to removing idolatry.

questions.question: True or False: Asa's heart was divided because he did not remove the high places during his reign.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 15:14 clarifies that although Asa did not remove the high places, his heart was perfect with the LORD all his days, showing his devotion was wholehearted despite incomplete reforms.

questions.question: True or False: Asa sent treasures from the house of the LORD and the king's house to Benhadad to maintain peace with Baasha king of Israel.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: According to 1 Kings 15:18-19, Asa sent treasures to Benhadad to persuade him to break his league with Baasha, an act of strategic alliance rather than mere peacekeeping.

hard.title: 1 Kings Chapter 15 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 1 Kings Chapter 15.

questions.question: Who conspired against Nadab king of Israel and killed him at Gibbethon?
questions.correctAnswer: Baasha
questions.explanation: Baasha conspired against Nadab and killed him at Gibbethon as recorded in 1 Kings 15:27.

questions.question: How long did Baasha reign over all Israel from Tirzah?
questions.correctAnswer: 24 years
questions.explanation: Baasha reigned for twenty-four years in Tirzah according to 1 Kings 15:33.

questions.question: Why did Baasha destroy the house of Jeroboam completely?
options: Because of the sins of Jeroboam which provoked the LORD
To stop Asa's alliance with Syria
questions.correctAnswer: Because of the sins of Jeroboam which provoked the LORD
questions.explanation: Baasha destroyed the house of Jeroboam because of Jeroboam's sins that provoked God as stated in 1 Kings 15:29-30.

questions.question: What was the relationship between Nadab's reign and Asa's reign in Judah?
options: Nadab began to reign in the second year of Asa's reign
questions.correctAnswer: Nadab began to reign in the second year of Asa's reign
questions.explanation: Nadab began to reign over Israel in the second year of Asa king of Judah as mentioned in 1 Kings 15:25.

questions.question: Which king sent a present of silver and gold to Benhadad king of Syria to break a league with Baasha?
questions.correctAnswer: Asa
questions.explanation: Asa sent silver and gold to Benhadad king of Syria to break his alliance with Baasha as recorded in 1 Kings 15:18-19.

questions.question: What cities did Benhadad attack after receiving gifts from Asa?
options: Ijon, Dan, Abelbethmaachah, and all Cinneroth
questions.correctAnswer: Ijon, Dan, Abelbethmaachah, and all Cinneroth
questions.explanation: Benhadad attacked Ijon, Dan, Abelbethmaachah, and all Cinneroth as stated in 1 Kings 15:20.

questions.question: What did Asa do with the stones and timber taken from Ramah?
questions.correctAnswer: Built Geba and Mizpah
questions.explanation: Asa used the stones and timber from Ramah to build Geba and Mizpah as described in 1 Kings 15:22.

questions.question: True or False: Baasha reigned peacefully with Asa king of Judah without any wars during their reigns.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: There was war between Asa and Baasha king of Israel all their days as noted in 1 Kings 15:32.

questions.question: True or False: The phrase 'walked in the way of Jeroboam' in 1 Kings 15:34 indicates Baasha continued Jeroboam's sinful practices.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 'Walked in the way of Jeroboam' means Baasha followed Jeroboam's sinful example as explained in 1 Kings 15:34.

questions.question: Which prophetic servant's word did Baasha fulfill by smiting the house of Jeroboam?
questions.correctAnswer: Ahijah the Shilonite
questions.explanation: Baasha's destruction of Jeroboam's house fulfilled the word spoken by Ahijah the Shilonite as recorded in 1 Kings 15:29.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word translated as 'league' in 1 Kings 15:19 imply in the context of Asa's strategy?
questions.correctAnswer: A political alliance or treaty
questions.explanation: The Hebrew term for 'league' indicates a political alliance or treaty, which Asa sought to break between Baasha and Benhadad (1 Kings 15:19).

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently used in 1 Kings 15:29-30, where Baasha's actions fulfill a prophecy?
questions.correctAnswer: Foreshadowing
questions.explanation: The passage uses foreshadowing by showing Baasha fulfilling earlier prophecy about the destruction of Jeroboam's house (1 Kings 15:29-30).

questions.question: How does the conflict between Asa and Baasha in 1 Kings 15 reflect the broader theme of Israel's divided kingdom in the Old Testament?
options: It exemplifies the ongoing strife between Israel and Judah after Solomon's reign
It shows a period of peace and unity
It signifies the end of Israel's monarchy
It represents the alliance between northern and southern kingdoms
questions.correctAnswer: It exemplifies the ongoing strife between Israel and Judah after Solomon's reign
questions.explanation: The wars between Asa and Baasha illustrate the persistent rivalry and division between the northern and southern kingdoms following Solomon's reign, a key theme in the Old Testament (1 Kings 15:32).

questions.question: Which other Old Testament passage echoes the theme of divine judgment on Jeroboam’s house as seen in 1 Kings 15?
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 14:10-11 prophesies the downfall of Jeroboam’s house, which is echoed in the judgment fulfilled by Baasha in 1 Kings 15:29-30.

questions.question: How does 1 Kings 15 relate to New Testament teachings about leadership and obedience to God?
options: It shows the consequences of disobedience, aligning with Hebrews 13:17 on obedience to leaders
It is unrelated to New Testament teachings
It encourages self-rule without divine guidance
questions.correctAnswer: It shows the consequences of disobedience, aligning with Hebrews 13:17 on obedience to leaders
questions.explanation: The chapter illustrates consequences for kings who disobey God, which aligns with New Testament teachings like Hebrews 13:17 emphasizing submission to God-honoring leaders.

theological.title: 1 Kings Chapter 15 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 1 Kings Chapter 15 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine is illustrated by the LORD giving Abijam a lamp in Jerusalem for David's sake, despite Abijam's imperfect heart?
questions.correctAnswer: Doctrine of Divine Mercy
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 15:4 shows God's mercy in preserving David's lineage through Abijam despite his sins, emphasizing God's grace rather than strict justice. This illustrates divine mercy rather than justification by works or predestination.

questions.question: Which attribute of God is most clearly revealed by the ongoing war between Rehoboam and Jeroboam throughout their reigns?
options: God's Patience in enduring human rebellion
God's Wrath against only foreign nations
questions.correctAnswer: God's Patience in enduring human rebellion
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 15:6 indicates ongoing conflict due to sin and rebellion, yet God allows these events to unfold, showing His longsuffering patience despite persistent human disobedience.

questions.question: How does Asa’s removal of idols and the sodomites illustrate the doctrine of sanctification?
options: Sanctification as a continual process of purifying from sin
questions.correctAnswer: Sanctification as a continual process of purifying from sin
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 15:12-13 describe Asa’s active efforts to remove sinful practices and idols, demonstrating sanctification as an ongoing, purposeful cleansing process in the believer's life.

questions.question: What theological significance does Asa’s heart being 'perfect with the LORD all his days' have despite incomplete removal of high places?
options: God values sincere devotion even when imperfect obedience is present
God requires absolute perfection in all external worship
God only judges kings by their military success
God ignores partial obedience if the heart is pure
questions.correctAnswer: God values sincere devotion even when imperfect obedience is present
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 15:14 portrays God's acceptance of Asa's sincere and devoted heart despite some incomplete reforms, highlighting the primacy of inward faithfulness over external perfection.

questions.question: What does Asa’s use of temple treasures to secure an alliance reveal about the interplay of faith and human responsibility?
options: God’s providence works through human means and decisions
Faith excludes any human effort or resource use
Human plans always contradict God’s will
Only prayer, not action, is effective in crises
questions.correctAnswer: God’s providence works through human means and decisions
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 15:18-19 shows Asa using resources to form an alliance, indicating that faith in God includes responsible use of means, aligning with divine providence working through human agency.

questions.question: Synthesis: How do verses 15:11 and 15:34 together teach about the consequences of walking in God’s way versus the way of sin?
options: Right walking with God leads to blessing; sin leads to judgment and downfall
All kings are equally blessed regardless of their actions
Sinful kings receive immediate forgiveness without consequences
Walking in God's way has no impact on a king's reign
questions.correctAnswer: Right walking with God leads to blessing; sin leads to judgment and downfall
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 15:11 praises Asa for doing right, whereas 15:34 condemns Baasha for evil, showing a clear theological principle that obedience brings favor and sin brings judgment (cf. Deut 28).

questions.question: What does the destruction of Jeroboam’s house by Baasha fulfill in terms of divine prophecy and judgment?
options: Fulfillment of the LORD's spoken judgment through Ahijah the Shilonite
Random political assassination with no divine purpose
A man-made conspiracy unrelated to sin
A sign of God's indifference to Israel's kings
questions.correctAnswer: Fulfillment of the LORD's spoken judgment through Ahijah the Shilonite
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 15:29 references the fulfillment of God’s judgment pronounced by the prophet Ahijah against Jeroboam’s house, illustrating God's sovereignty in executing justice.

questions.question: Narrative arc: How does Asa’s reign (verses 15:9-24) contribute to the redemptive history of Israel’s monarchy?
options: It exemplifies faithful leadership that points forward to Christ’s righteous kingship
It shows total apostasy with no hope of restoration
It documents the end of David’s lineage
questions.correctAnswer: It exemplifies faithful leadership that points forward to Christ’s righteous kingship
questions.explanation: Asa’s faithfulness and reforms (1 Kings 15:11, 15:14) highlight themes of covenant loyalty and sanctification, foreshadowing the perfect kingship of Christ who fulfills David’s line.

questions.question: Doctrine: What doctrine is demonstrated by the continuous wars between Israel and Judah kings in this chapter?
options: Doctrine of Divine Judgment on persistent sin and division
Doctrine of Universal Peace during the monarchy
Doctrine of Kingdom Unity under Jeroboam
Doctrine of Salvation by Military Might
questions.correctAnswer: Doctrine of Divine Judgment on persistent sin and division
questions.explanation: Verses such as 15:6, 15:16, and 15:32 show ongoing wars tied to sin and rebellion, illustrating God's judgment on the divided kingdom for disobedience (cf. Judges 2:20-22).

questions.question: Synthesis: Considering verses 15:5 and 15:30, what overarching theological truth do they reveal about sin and its corporate impact?
options: Individual sin leads to corporate national sin and divine provocation
Sin only affects the individual with no broader consequences
God overlooks corporate sin if the king is righteous
Corporate sin is unrelated to individual leadership
questions.correctAnswer: Individual sin leads to corporate national sin and divine provocation
questions.explanation: Verse 15:5 notes David’s near-perfect obedience with one sin affecting him; 15:30 shows Jeroboam’s sin caused Israel to sin, revealing how leaders' sins provoke national judgment.

questions.question: Attribute of God: Which divine attribute is highlighted by God’s continuing covenant promise to David’s line despite the failure of his descendants?
questions.correctAnswer: God’s Faithfulness
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 15:4 shows that for David's sake, God preserves his lineage and establishes Jerusalem, demonstrating His unwavering faithfulness to His covenant promises (cf. 2 Sam 7).

questions.question: Apologetics: Sceptics claim that God’s involvement in human wars shows He is unjust and violent. What does 1 Kings 15:17-21 actually teach about God’s use of political events?
options: God sovereignly uses political events to fulfill His purposes and execute judgment
God randomly causes wars without moral reason
God supports all kings regardless of their sin
God is uninvolved in earthly affairs
questions.correctAnswer: God sovereignly uses political events to fulfill His purposes and execute judgment
questions.explanation: Verses 17-21 show Baasha’s military actions thwarted by Asa’s alliance, revealing God’s sovereign orchestration of political events to accomplish His righteous plans and judgments.

questions.question: Narrative arc: How does the removal of Maachah as queen mother for idolatry (15:13) contribute to the biblical theme of covenant purity?
options: It underscores the necessity of purging idolatry to maintain covenant relationship
It shows that family relationships override covenant obedience
It implies idol worship is acceptable in secret
It indicates that political alliances are more important than faithfulness
questions.correctAnswer: It underscores the necessity of purging idolatry to maintain covenant relationship
questions.explanation: Removing Maachah (1 Kings 15:13) for idol worship illustrates the serious threat of idolatry to covenant purity and God’s demand for holiness among leadership (cf. Deut 12:29-31).

questions.question: Doctrine: The chronicling of kings’ deeds in the 'book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah/Israel' (verses 7, 31, 23) teaches what about biblical historiography?
options: The Bible presents history as purposeful narrative revealing God’s dealings
The Bible focuses only on laws, not history
The Bible records only positive deeds
questions.correctAnswer: The Bible presents history as purposeful narrative revealing God’s dealings
questions.explanation: References in 1 Kings 15:7, 15:23, and 15:31 show biblical history is selective, emphasizing God’s covenant actions and moral evaluation of kings, presenting history as theological narrative.

questions.question: Synthesis: What combined doctrinal insight do verses 15:24 and 15:28 offer about the continuity of God’s covenant promises despite political upheaval?
options: God sustains His covenant through successive generations even amid violent regime changes
God abandons His covenant when kings are killed
Covenant promises are only for Israel, not Judah
questions.correctAnswer: God sustains His covenant through successive generations even amid violent regime changes
questions.explanation: 15:24 shows Asa’s son Jehoshaphat succeeding him, while 15:28 records Baasha’s violent takeover, indicating God's covenant line persists despite political violence (cf. Gen 17:7).
